clue.text: See 20
Plant producing underwear is backed by state

parts.note: bras are items of underwear

indicators.note: backed here means the little word before it is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of California

explanation.surface: A plant that somehow yields lingerie, propped up by a state subsidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the word 'is' round. 'state' is California by its two-letter postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the botanical genus of cabbages, sprouts and their relatives, so it names a kind of plant.

clue.text: Gun dog bounds off, free

indicators.note: bounds are the outer limits, so taking them off leaves the inner letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A gundog bounds away, released from its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounds off' looks like the dog leaping away; it strips the two G's from the ends of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or a fastening is to free or release it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: B movie opening and closing cinema presentation to create mood

indicators.note: a presentation is a new arrangement or staging, so the letters are set out afresh
the opening and closing letters of the words are taken, that is the first and the very last

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A B movie whose opening and closing scenes set the mood of the cinema showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening and closing' takes B and E, the first and last letters of 'B movie'; 'presentation' rearranges BE with CINEMA. Bloggers thought taking ends across two words a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the atmosphere or feeling of a place, which is its mood.

clue.text: Team batting at the Queen's pleasure?

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricket team batting at the pleasure of the Queen, as if in a royal match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detained at Her Majesty's pleasure' is the British legal phrase for an indefinite prison sentence, so the question mark points to being in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside is slang for being in prison, which is where someone held at the monarch's pleasure ends up.

clue.text: Tormentor who would make Shelley more smart, when read out?

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the words are judged by how they sound rather than how they are spelt

parts.note: the Romantic poet Percy Bysshe Shelley gives Percy, and more smart is acuter, sharper

explanation.surface: A tormentor who would sharpen the poet Shelley's wits.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley's first name, Percy, and ACUTER said together run close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A persecutor harasses and torments others, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: A grand entrance in residence gains respect

indicators.note: making an entrance into something puts these letters inside it

parts.note: a home is a residence
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A grand doorway on a house earns admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance in' places A and G inside HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay homage is to show public honour and esteem, so homage is a form of respect.

clue.text: Rex comes off wagon at saloon opening times!

indicators.note: when the king comes off the cart his letter is taken away from it

parts.note: a dray is a low wagon, as used by brewers
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: the opening of the word means its first letter

explanation.surface: A king climbs down from the brewer's cart just as the bar opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes off' takes R out of DRAY, leaving DAY. 'opening' gives S. A bar-room and a brewer's dray suit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Days can mean times or an era, as in 'in my days' meaning in my time.

clue.text: Body protection for one who's paid to slice one

indicators.note: slicing into a word cuts it open so another piece goes in the middle

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'
a pro is a professional, someone paid for the work

explanation.surface: Armour for a hired swordsman who is paid to carve up an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' does double duty in the surface: the first is part of 'one who's paid', a professional; the second is the article AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment worn over the front of the body to protect clothing.

clue.text: Atoms spinning round in north-eastern state

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the mixed letters wrap the next pieces
spinning particles whirl about, so the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Atoms whirl about inside some northeastern American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north-eastern state' reads as the definition, but Minnesota is in the Midwest; 'north-eastern' only supplies two letters, and 'spinning' mixes ATOMS to MSOTA around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty United States, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Right-wing leader — poor soul's in 60s' wear!

indicators.note: the mixed letters go into the other word

parts.note: the miniskirt, or mini, was a fashion item of the 1960s

indicators.note: poor letters are badly formed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A right-wing leader pictured as a sorry figure dressed in a sixties miniskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like pity for the soul, but it signals the rearrangement; 'in' sets those letters inside the skirt after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini was the Fascist dictator of Italy, a famously right-wing leader.

clue.text: Protective wear clashes

definitions.meaning: cloth coverings worn over the shoe and ankle to protect them

explanation.surface: Protective clothing collides, or the people wearing it come to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both old-fashioned gaiters for the ankle and minor squabbles.

clue.text: Tunic or nightie? Not tight, that is a fabulous creation

indicators.note: not means without, so these letters are taken away from the phrase

parts.note: the answer also runs in plain sight across these words, a coincidence commenters spotted; the setter meant letters to be taken away
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Choosing between a tunic and a loose nightie, not a tight one, produces a fairytale garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes the letters of 'tight', scattered through the phrase (one at the front, the rest inside 'nightie'), plus the closing IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a mythical horned horse, a creature of fable rather than fact.

clue.text: Saul certainly suppresses corrupting influence

indicators.note: the phrase holds down and conceals the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: The biblical Saul plainly crushes a source of moral decay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is a festering sore, and figuratively any corrupting influence that eats away from within.

clue.text: Tentatively propose sin as a tyrant's thing

indicators.note: something put forward tentatively is not yet fixed, so the letters are open to rearrangement

explanation.surface: Hesitantly suggesting a sin as the sort of thing a despot would do.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppression, the cruel exercise of power over people, is what a tyrant practises.

clue.text: Confiscate drugs (cocaine) with passion

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so ES are drugs
C is slang shorthand for cocaine
heat means intensity of feeling, passion

explanation.surface: Police seize narcotics, cocaine included, with fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: To escheat is an old legal term for property reverting to the state or lord, so to confiscate or forfeit it.

clue.text: Start to tuck in old hat label

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: tile is dated slang for a hat

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Begin by tucking a tag into a worn-out hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like 'dated', but TILE is old slang for a hat; 'in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a name or heading given to something, so it serves as a label.

clue.text: A hand needed to secure second military bar

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast, so one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: giving someone a hand means a round of applause, a clap

explanation.surface: A helping hand is needed to fasten a second bar on a soldier's medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts S inside CLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp is a bar fixed to a military medal ribbon, naming the campaign or action.

clue.text: Rib woman when Guardian has leader cut

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and cutting it removes it from the front

parts.note: the Guardian newspaper speaks of itself as 'we', so 'Guardian has' is we've

explanation.surface: A dig at a woman as the Guardian's lead story is axed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader cut' drops the W of WE'VE. In Genesis, Eve was made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, was formed from one of Adam's ribs.

clue.text: Prepare to fight graduate in US city, having lost head

indicators.note: the graduate letters go inside the shortened city name
losing its head means the city's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Seattle is a city in Washington state
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A graduate in an American city, having lost their head, gets ready for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost head' turns SEATTLE into EATTLE. A Bachelor of Medicine is the graduate here, not the usual BA.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to draw up troops in battle array, so to ready them for combat.

clue.text: Art form involved with origins of the underworld and source of rainbows?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so all these letters are mixed together
the origin of a word is its starting point, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: An art form drawing on underworld myths and the source of rainbows sounds like mythology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' gives T and U, which 'involved with' mixes with ARTFORM. The question mark warns that the rainbows are fish, not arcs of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainbow trout are raised in fish farms, so such a farm is where rainbows come from.

clue.text: Round sort of canine, a native of Polynesia?

parts.note: the round shape of the letter O

indicators.note: sort as a verb means rearrange, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rotund breed of dog, perhaps native to the South Pacific islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is part of Oceania, so a Polynesian native is an example of an Oceanian, hence the question mark.

clue.text: With which to do a chemical test on a public toilet? Not quite

definitions.text: With which to do a chemical test

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Gents is a British name for a men's public lavatory

explanation.surface: A chemist asks what to use for testing in a public loo, getting it nearly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is RE, 'regarding'. 'Not quite' cuts the last S from GENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added to a sample to detect or measure a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Beastly male, one covered in dye

indicators.note: being covered in something means it wraps round, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it
a means one

explanation.surface: A brutish man, one smeared all over in dye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' is the adjective sense of the answer. Anil is an indigo dye, rare outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means of the body or brutish, like a beast.

clue.text: Approach of one contralto after tense performance

indicators.note: the later pieces come after the earlier ones in the answer

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
an act is a performance on stage
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the musical abbreviation for contralto

explanation.surface: A contralto singer's approach after a nervous performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like a nervy adjective; it is T. The singer comes 'after' T and ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned method or way of tackling something, an approach.

clue.text: Be sure to turn round Monsieur's tongue

indicators.note: the mixed letters wrap round the next piece
turning the letters about rearranges them

parts.note: M. is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: Remember to turn round and hear a Frenchman's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' rearranges BESURE to BURESE; 'round' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Burmese is the language of Myanmar, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Hippy gatherings — not very English, showing genital area!

indicators.note: not means leaving out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: love-ins were hippy gatherings of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Hippy festivals, hardly English in manner, where people bare all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes V and E from LOVEINS. 'Hippy' tempts one toward hips, near the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The loins are the region of the hips and groin, used euphemistically for the genitals.

clue.text: Person of note from Grease turned up with Newton-John at last

indicators.note: in a down clue turning a word up means reading it from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: oil is grease, a lubricant

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A star from the film Grease appeared with Olivia Newton-John at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Grease is the 1978 musical starring Olivia Newton-John, but here it is just OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion is a celebrity, a person of note, as in a social lion.

clue.text: Italy cutting canal to a distressed European region

indicators.note: cutting into the mixed letters puts this one inside them
distressed means battered, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Italy builds a canal to some unhappy European area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges CANALTOA, and 'cutting' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is an autonomous region of north-eastern Spain.

clue.text: Lots of blades involved in making this cloth

definitions.meaning: an expanse of grass, many blades together
a fine linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Many sword blades go into weaving this fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a grassy garden area and a fine sheer fabric.

clue.text: Ex-vice president good to go once more

indicators.note: letting a letter go removes it from the name

parts.note: Spiro Agnew was US vice president under Nixon

explanation.surface: A former vice president is ready to run again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' takes G out of AGNEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means again, afresh, once more.

clue.text: Speech-related examination includes a trio composition

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

indicators.note: a composition arranges parts anew, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An oral exam includes performing a piece written for a trio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges ATRIO to ATORI. 'examination' is the spoken kind, an oral.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorial means relating to oratory, the art of public speaking.

clue.text: Maybe the right sort of wife (robust)

parts.note: hale means healthy and robust

explanation.surface: Perhaps just the right kind of wife: a sturdy one.
explanation.walkthrough: The right whale is a species of baleen whale, so 'right sort' is an example, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The right whale is one sort of whale, so the right sort is an instance of the answer.
